Read docs/TASK_P21b_deckcheck.md sections 2.2 (src/planner/stubTrees.ts) and 4. Write one file src/planner/stubTrees.ts: `export interface TreeLanguage`, `export interface StubTree` and `export function stubTrees(cards: Card[], generations: string[][], stubDir: string, stubs: string[], languages: TreeLanguage[]): StubTree[]` exactly as section 2.2 shows, importing `path` from "node:path" (path.posix only) and `import type { Card } from "../cards/types.js"`. Pure: no process, no console, no Date, no Math.random, no file read, no other node: module; the inputs are never changed. Write no test file: a probe tests you and a judge writes the example tests.

## Function Stub Trees

Per card of a deck, the tree its first attempt compiles on, the gate's stubs in place.

Behaviour: stubTrees(cards, generations, stubDir, stubs, languages: Tree Language[]): for every generation index g and every id of generations[g], in order, the card of cards with that customId (none → skipped); acceptance = its text, "" when null. config: for the first language (in languages order) whose config is not null and whose heredoc the acceptance writes — a line exactly `cat > $P/<config> <<'<TAG>'`, then the lines up to the next line exactly <TAG> — {name: that config, text: those lines "\n"-joined}; that language is the card's. None → config null and the card's language is the first language whose extensions hold the extension (path.posix.extname) of the card's first target, or null. exports = the acceptance's lines that, trimmed, match /^export [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/, trimmed, in order. With a config: for every card of generations[0..g-1] (flattened in order, ids with no card skipped) and then the card itself, every target whose extension the language's extensions hold and that is not yet stubbed: in stubs → stubs map target → path.posix.join(stubDir, target); else into missing, once. The card's generation siblings are never stubbed: its first attempt sees them as its config leaves them, or as on disk. Without a config, stubs {} and missing []. → Stub Tree {card, generation: g, language: its id or null, exports, config, stubs, own: a copy of the card's targets, missing}. The inputs are never changed.

Steps:
- reads: Deck
- produces: Stub Tree

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given stub.cards.json; generations [["a", "n", "t", "p"], ["b", "c", "v", "u"], ["j"]]; stubDir "decks/q9/_stubs"; stubs ["calc/a.go", "calc/a_examples_test.go", "calc/b.go", "extra/z.go", "report/c.go", "src/t.ts", "tests/t.test.ts"]; languages L = [{id "typescript", extensions [".ts", ".tsx"], config "tsconfig.card.json"}, {id "python", extensions [".py", ".pyi"], config null}, {id "go", extensions [".go"], config "full.json"}]; when stubTrees; then equal to stub.trees.json["1"]: 9 trees in generation order a, n, t, p, b, c, v, u, j; a go, config full.json, exports ["export NO_COLOR=1 CI=1", "export GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off"], stubs {"calc/a.go": "decks/q9/_stubs/calc/a.go"}; n go (by extension), config null; t typescript, stubs src/t.ts and tests/t.test.ts; p python, config null; b missing ["calc/n.go", "calc/b_test.go"]; v go, config null; u typescript, missing ["tests/u.test.ts"]; j stubs calc/a.go, calc/b.go, report/c.go, calc/a_examples_test.go, missing ["calc/n.go", "calc/b_test.go", "calc/v.go"] (ref: tests/fixtures/planner/stub.cards.json, tests/fixtures/planner/stub.trees.json (key "1"))
2. given stub.cards.json, generations [["a"], ["zz", "j"]], stubDir "/abs/st", stubs ["calc/a_examples_test.go"], languages L; when stubTrees; then equal to stub.trees.json["2"]: a (0) stubs {}, missing ["calc/a.go"]; j (1) stubs {"calc/a_examples_test.go": "/abs/st/calc/a_examples_test.go"}, missing ["calc/a.go"]
3. given stub.cards.json, generations [["a", "t", "u"]], stubDir "st", stubs ["calc/a.go", "src/t.ts", "tests/t.test.ts", "tests/u.test.ts"], languages [the go entry of L only]; when stubTrees; then equal to stub.trees.json["3"]: a go with stubs {"calc/a.go": "st/calc/a.go"}; t and u language null, config null, stubs {}, missing []

Data Deck: The loaded backlog.
Schema:
{
  "cards": "Card[] in file order",
  "externalDependsOn": "string[] — dependsOn names not in the deck"
}

Data Stub Tree: One card's first-attempt tree for the deck check.
Schema:
{ card: string; generation: number; language: string | null; exports: string[]; config: { name: string; text: string } | null; stubs: Record<string, string>; own: string[]; missing: string[] }

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; Run Mutants writes only through acceptance's Restore Snapshot; Review Command is the reviewer layer's one node:fs file (the record, the map and scout.json read, the review written), the environment a parameter, no clock and no model call (P14b). debt spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance and git's Run Git, reads the deck file, the card's files and the run archive through node:fs, no clock and no model call; the environment is a parameter (P17). scaffold reads the template folders and writes the new project through node:fs (node:url only to find the package root from its own module file), spawns nothing, reads no clock and no environment (P18).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

Write one file src/acceptance/treeCheck.ts: `export interface TreeRun`, `export interface TreeInput`, `export function findBreaks(output: string, fileLine: string, own: string[]): string[]` and `export function treeCheck(root: string, input: TreeInput, env: Record<string, string>, timeoutMs: number): TreeRun` exactly as section 2.2 shows, importing spawnSync from "node:child_process", fs from "node:fs", os from "node:os", path from "node:path". The child's environment is exactly the env parameter; never read process.env; no console; stdio "ignore" (the output goes to a file, so a killed shell's children never hold a pipe). ## Function Tree Check

A copy of the tree with stubs in place, one compile step run in it; and the file:line lines of an output.

Behaviour: treeCheck(root, {card, exports, config: {name, text}, stubs, command}, env, timeoutMs): a fresh directory D under os.tmpdir(); T = D/t holds a copy of root's entries (symbolic links copied as links) but ".git", ".morph", "probe" and "node_modules" — a node_modules of root becomes a symbolic link to its real path; every stubs entry target → stub copies root/stub over T/target (parents created); config.text + "\n" is written to T/probe/<card>/<config.name>; then `/bin/sh -c` with the exports lines, "P='<T>/probe/<card>'" and "{ " + command with every "{config}" replaced by "\"$P/<config.name>\"" + "\n} > '<D>/output.txt' 2>&1", "\n"-joined, cwd T, environment exactly env, no stdio pipe, a timeout of timeoutMs; D removed always. → Tree Run {exit: the status (null when timed out or killed), timedOut, output: the output file's text ("" when absent) with every "<T>/" removed}. findBreaks(output, fileLine, own), pure: re = new RegExp(fileLine); every line of output but a blank one, one starting with "#" and one starting with white space (a continuation), trimmed: matching re → skipped when group 1 (the file) is in own, else group 1 + group 2; not matching → the line as it stands. Once each, sorted (JavaScript's default sort).

Steps:
- produces: Tree Run

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given the texts of tests/fixtures/acceptance/treeOutput.json; findBreaks(go, Go's fileLine, ["supervisor/loop.go"]); (typescript, TypeScript's fileLine, ["src/units/convert.ts"]); (go, TypeScript's fileLine, []); when findBreaks; then ["daemon/daemon.go:9:81: not enough arguments in call to d.Loop.Exited", "go: updates to go.mod needed; to update it:", "mcp/session.go:6:2: package morphlite/supervisor is not in std", "supervisor/guard.go:20:23: l.Resumes undefined (type *Loop has no field or method Resumes)"]; then ["error TS5083: Cannot read file '/x/tsconfig.json'.", "src/report/line.ts(1,17): error TS2724: '\"../units/convert.js\"' has no exported member named 'toMeters'. Did you mean 'toMetres'?", "tests/report/line.examples.test.ts(5,44): error TS2554: Expected 3 arguments, but got 2."]; then 7 lines kept whole, "vet: " prefixes included (ref: tests/fixtures/acceptance/treeOutput.json)
2. given a tmp root holding a copy of tests/fixtures/acceptance/tree (module example.com/vq: b/b.go Old, a/a.go calling b.Old, _stubs/b/b.go New); exports [G = "export GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOWORK=off GOCACHE=\"${GOCACHE:-/tmp/morph/go-build}\" GOPATH=\"${GOPATH:-/tmp/morph/go}\""]; card "k1"; Go's command; env {PATH}; timeout 60000: config full.json {"Replace":{}} with stubs {"b/b.go": "_stubs/b/b.go"}; then {"Replace":{"a/a.go":""}}; then {"Replace":{}} and no stub; when treeCheck; then {exit: 1, timedOut: false, output: "# example.com/vq/a\na/a.go:6:25: undefined: b.Old\n# example.com/vq/a\nvet: a/a.go:6:25: undefined: b.Old\n"}; then {exit: 0, timedOut: false, output: ""}; then {exit: 0, timedOut: false, output: ""}; the root unchanged (ref: tests/fixtures/acceptance/tree/)
3. given that root plus .git/HEAD, node_modules/q/ and probe/old/; card "k2", exports ["export Q9=-mod=vendor"], config c.json "{\"q\": 9}", stubs {"b/b.go": "_stubs/b/b.go"}, command 'echo "a.go:1:1: $Q9 $(cat {config}) $(head -3 b/b.go | tail -1)"; ls -a; echo "$(pwd)/x.go:2:2: abs"; readlink node_modules >/dev/null && echo linked'; then card "k3", command "echo started; sleep 3; echo late", timeout 700; when treeCheck; then {exit: 0, timedOut: false, output: "a.go:1:1: -mod=vendor {\"q\": 9} // New is the API after the change.\n.\n..\n_stubs\na\nb\ngo.mod\nnode_modules\nprobe\nx.go:2:2: abs\nlinked\n"}; then {exit: null, timedOut: true, output: "started\n"} in under 3000 ms

Data Tree Run: What one compile step in a stub tree returned.
Schema:
{ exit: number | null, timedOut: boolean, output: string }

## Function Tree Profiles

Per language, how deck check compiles a stub tree and how a file:line line of its tools reads.

Behaviour: src/language/treeProfiles.ts: TREE_PROFILES, one Tree Profile per profile of PROFILES, in the same order, pure data; treeProfileFor(id) → the entry with that id, else null. The strings below are JavaScript string literals. typescript: config "tsconfig.card.json", command "node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p {config}", fileLine "^(\\S+?\\.tsx?)(\\(\\d+,\\d+\\).*)$"; python: config null, command null (no compile or typecheck step), fileLine "^(\\S+?\\.pyi?)(:\\d+.*)$"; go: config "full.json", command "go build -overlay {config} ./... ; go vet -overlay {config} ./...", fileLine "^(?:vet: )?(?:\\./)?(\\S+?\\.go)(:\\d+.*)$". config is the file a card's acceptance writes into $P that sets what its compile stage sees; {config} is that file's path; group 1 of fileLine is the file, group 2 the rest of the line from the position on. Text only, never run here.

Steps:
- produces: Tree Profile

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given treeProfileFor("typescript"), treeProfileFor("python"), treeProfileFor("go"), treeProfileFor("rust"); when looked up; then the three entries as the behavior writes them, each id equal to a PROFILES id in the same order; then null
2. given new RegExp(each fileLine) on "src/a/b.ts(12,5): error TS2304: x", "vet: ./pkg/q.go:3:7: y", "pkg/q.go:3: z", "tests/test_a.py:9: AssertionError", " src/a.ts(1,1): continuation"; when matched; then typescript: ["src/a/b.ts", "(12,5): error TS2304: x"] on the first only; go: ["pkg/q.go", ":3:7: y"] and ["pkg/q.go", ":3: z"]; python: ["tests/test_a.py", ":9: AssertionError"]; no fileLine matches the indented line

Schema:
{ id: string; fileLine: string; config: string | null; command: string | null }

## Function Check Builds

Every card's stub tree of a deck compiled by its language's step; the lines outside its own targets.

Behaviour: checkBuilds(root, deckPath, deck, generations, env). stubDir = path.posix.join(path.posix.dirname(deckPath), "_stubs"); not a directory under root (path.resolve(root, stubDir)) → null. Else stubs = every regular file under it, paths relative to it joined by "/" (a symbolic link is not followed), sorted; languages = PROFILES in order, each {id, extensions, config: treeProfileFor(id)'s config (Tree Profiles)}; for every tree of Stub Trees(deck.cards, generations, stubDir, stubs, languages), in order, a Build Check {card, generation, language, stubbed: the count of its stubs, missing, breaks, note}: language null → breaks [], note "no language profile claims <own[0], or "no target">: not built"; its Tree Profile's command or config null → note "<id> has no compile or typecheck step: not built"; the tree's config null → note "the acceptance writes no $P/<the profile's config>: not built"; else note null and breaks = Find Breaks(Tree Check(root, {card, exports, config, stubs, command: the profile's}, env, 120000).output, the profile's fileLine, own), followed, when it timed out, by "the compile step timed out after 120000 ms". A language with no step is said so, never skipped silently.

Steps:
- calls: Stub Trees
- uses: language
- uses: acceptance

Requirements:

env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; Run Mutants writes only through acceptance's Restore Snapshot; Review Command is the reviewer layer's one node:fs file (the record, the map and scout.json read, the review written), the environment a parameter, no clock and no model call (P14b). debt spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance and git's Run Git, reads the deck file, the card's files and the run archive through node:fs, no clock and no model call; the environment is a parameter (P17). scaffold reads the template folders and writes the new project through node:fs (node:url only to find the package root from its own module file), spawns nothing, reads no clock and no environment (P18).

Schema:
{ card: string; generation: number; language: string | null; stubbed: number; missing: string[]; breaks: string[]; note: string | null }

Callee Stub Trees: Per card of a deck, the tree its first attempt compiles on, the gate's stubs in place.
Behaviour: stubTrees(cards, generations, stubDir, stubs, languages: Tree Language[]): for every generation index g and every id of generations[g], in order, the card of cards with that customId (none → skipped); acceptance = its text, "" when null. config: for the first language (in languages order) whose config is not null and whose heredoc the acceptance writes — a line exactly `cat > $P/<config> <<'<TAG>'`, then the lines up to the next line exactly <TAG> — {name: that config, text: those lines "\n"-joined}; that language is the card's. None → config null and the card's language is the first language whose extensions hold the extension (path.posix.extname) of the card's first target, or null. exports = the acceptance's lines that, trimmed, match /^export [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/, trimmed, in order. With a config: for every card of generations[0..g-1] (flattened in order, ids with no card skipped) and then the card itself, every target whose extension the language's extensions hold and that is not yet stubbed: in stubs → stubs map target → path.posix.join(stubDir, target); else into missing, once. The card's generation siblings are never stubbed: its first attempt sees them as its config leaves them, or as on disk. Without a config, stubs {} and missing []. → Stub Tree {card, generation: g, language: its id or null, exports, config, stubs, own: a copy of the card's targets, missing}. The inputs are never changed.
